record.title: Shi–Shan conjecture for $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $P_b$ denote the path on $b$ vertices, and let $P_2\cup kP_1$ be the disjoint union of a two-vertex path and $k$ isolated vertices. A graph is **$t$-tough** if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every vertex set $S$ such that $G-S$ has at least two components; it is $r$-connected if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves it connected. A graph is $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $P_2\cup kP_1$.

**Shi–Shan conjecture.** Let $k\geq 4$ be an integer and let $G$ be a $1$-tough and $2k$-connected $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free graph. Then $G$ is hamiltonian.

The paper proves the analogous assertion with $4$-tough in place of $1$-tough, so the conjecture proposes that the toughness hypothesis can be weakened. The conjectured $1$-tough result remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Lingjuan Shi and Songling Shan, “A note on hamiltonian cycles in 4-tough (P_2kP_1)-free graphs”, arXiv:2202.06192 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06192

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Even-arity complete full tree local antimagic chromatic number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a complete full $t$-ary tree, meaning a rooted tree in which every nonleaf has exactly $t$ children and all leaves have the same depth. Let $l$ be the number of leaves and let $\chi_{la}(T)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number. **Even-arity complete full tree conjecture.** For every even integer $t\geq2$,

$$
\chi_{la}(T)=l+1.
$$

The paper explicitly states this conjecture as open; it would sharpen the established upper bound $\chi_{la}(T)\leq l+2$, while the equality is proved in the paper for odd $t$.
record.source_name: Martin Bača, Andrea Semaničová-Feňovčíková, Ruei-Ting Lai and Tao-Ming Wang, “On local antimagic vertex coloring for complete full t-ary trees”, arXiv:2204.04479 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04479

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Three-colorability conjecture for graphs with prescribed girth and no long odd holes
record.statement:
For each integer $\ell\ge 2$, let ${\cal G}_{\ell}$ be the family of graphs with girth $2\ell+1$ and with no odd holes of length at least $2\ell+3$.

**Three-colorability conjecture.** Every graph $G$ in any of these families satisfies

$$
\chi(G)\le 3\qquad\text{for each graph }G\in\bigcup_{\ell\ge 2}{\cal G}_{\ell}.
$$

The paper has already established a $4$-colorability bound for each ${\cal G}_{\ell}$ and notes that, assuming the conjecture for ${\cal G}_2$, it is reasonable to expect this stronger three-colorability statement for all $\ell\ge2$. The supplied material gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Di Wu, Baogang Xu and Yian Xu, “On coloring of graphs of girth 2l + 1 without longer odd holes”, arXiv:2204.06284 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06284

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2022). “Plummer and Zha presented counterexamples to Robertson's conjecture, and posed the following conjecture.”

record.title: Existence of smooth Mallows processes with non-total graph structure
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$. A **smooth Mallows process** is a process 
$$
{\mathcal{M}}={({\mathcal{M}}_t)_{t\in[0,\infty)}}
$$
 for which the associated graph group $\langle{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{M}}\rangle$ is defined, and let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the full graph group. **Existence conjecture.** For every $n\geq 3$, there exists a smooth Mallows process ${\mathcal{M}}$ such that 
$$
\langle{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{M}}\rangle\subsetneq{\mathcal{T}}.
$$
 This asks whether smooth Mallows processes can have strictly smaller graph structure than the full graph group; the source presents it as a possible direction for future work and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Benoît Corsini, “Continuous-time Mallows processes”, arXiv:2205.04967 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.04967

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2022). “Proving that this process indeed converges, and characterizing its distribution remains open.”

record.title: Horak–Rosa conjecture on realizable and admissible chord multisets
record.statement:
Consider $n$ equally spaced points on a circle and write $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. A multiset is represented as $[\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m]$, where $\ell_j$ counts chords of type $j$. Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the class of multisets satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^m\ell_j=n-1$. Let $\mathcal{A}_n\subseteq\mathcal{M}_n$ be the class satisfying, for every divisor $d$ of $n$,

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor m/d\rfloor}\ell_{jd}\leq n-d,
$$

and let $\mathcal{R}_n$ be the class of multisets associated with a path using every point exactly once. **Horak–Rosa conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
\mathcal{R}_n=\mathcal{A}_n.
$$

This generalizes Buratti's prime case and characterizes exactly which chord-type multisets are realizable by the necessary admissibility inequalities. The conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Brendan D. McKay and Tim Peters, “Paths through equally spaced points on a circle”, arXiv:2205.06004 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.06004

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2022). “Despite its simple statement, the conjecture remains open, though Mariusz Meszka confirmed it by computer for $n\leq 23$ .”

record.title: The 3-connected subgraph conjecture for chromatic-critical vertex pairs
record.statement: Let $m\ge4$, and let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number at least $m$. An **optimal coloring** of $G$ is a coloring using exactly $\chi(G)$ colors. **The chromatic-critical-pair conjecture.** If $G$ has nonadjacent vertices $u,v$ such that every optimal coloring of $G$ assigns different colors to $u$ and $v$, then $G$ contains a $3$-connected subgraph with chromatic number at least $m$. This conjecture is equivalent to the suspected equality $g(2,m)=m+1$ for all $m\ge4$, but the paper leaves it open.
record.source_name: Tung H. Nguyen, “Highly connected subgraphs with large chromatic number”, arXiv:2206.00561 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00561

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The removable-edge conjecture for surjective polymorphisms of reflexive cycles
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 4$, let $\mathbb{G}$ be an $n$-cycle, and let $f$ be a surjective homomorphism from a product of subpaths of $\mathbb{G}$ of length $n-2$ to $\mathbb{G}$. An **edge** $e$ of $\mathbb{G}$ is removable for $f$ if

$$
f(e')\neq e
$$

for every edge $e'$ of the product. **Removable-edge conjecture.** There exists a removable edge of $\mathbb{G}$ for $f$; equivalently, there exists an edge of $\mathbb{G}$ that can be removed while $f$ remains a homomorphism. This conjecture concerns the structure of surjective polymorphisms of reflexive cycles and the possibility of reducing the target cycle without destroying the homomorphism property. The supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Isabelle Larivière, Benoit Larose and David Emmanuel Pazmiño Pullas, “Surjective polymorphisms of reflexive cycles”, arXiv:2206.11390 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11390

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Tomon’s stability conjecture beyond the proven range
record.statement:
Let $t\geq2$, let $0<p\leq p_0(t)$, and let $\mathcal G\subset 2^{[n]}$ be a **3-wise $t$-intersecting family**, meaning that the intersection of any three members has size at least $t$. Define

$$
p_0(t)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{4t+9}-1}
$$

and, for $i=0,1,2$,

$$
\mathcal F_i^t=\{F\subset[n]:|F\cap[t+3i]|\geq t+2i\}.
$$

**Tomon’s conjecture.** If

$$
\mu_p(\mathcal G)>\max\left\{\frac12p^t,\,\mu_p(\mathcal F_1^t),\,\mu_p(\mathcal F_2^t)\right\},
$$

then $\mathcal G\subset\mathcal F$ for some $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F_0^t$.

The paper proves the corresponding stability result for $t\geq241$ and conjectures this stronger formulation for every $t\geq2$.
record.source_name: Norihide Tokushige, “Strong stability of 3-wise t-intersecting families”, arXiv:2304.13466 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13466

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

record.title: The tensor square conjecture for symmetric partitions
record.statement:
Let $g(\lambda,\lambda,\mu)$ be a Kronecker coefficient, and let $\mathbb{S}_\lambda$ denote the irreducible $S_n$-module indexed by the partition $\lambda$. **Tensor square conjecture.** For every $n\geq9$ there exists a symmetric partition $\lambda\vdash n$ such that

$$
\mathbb{S}_\lambda\otimes\mathbb{S}_\lambda
$$

contains every irreducible $S_n$-module; equivalently, $g(\lambda,\lambda,\mu)>0$ for all $\mu\vdash n$.

This generalizes Saxl's question about tensor squares and is part of the study of positivity of Kronecker coefficients. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Greta Panova, “Computational Complexity in Algebraic Combinatorics”, arXiv:2306.17511 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17511

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2023). “This was the first conjecture to be disproved.”

record.title: The bounded generic-base-gap conjecture for finite Morley rank actions
record.statement:
Let $(G,S)$ be a definably primitive permutation group of finite Morley rank. Let $b(G,S)$ be the minimal cardinality of a base, and let $b^1(G,S)$ be the least positive integer $n$ such that $S^n$ contains a generic subset all of whose tuples are bases. **Bounded generic-base-gap conjecture.** There is a natural number $d$ such that

$$
b^1(G,S)-b(G,S)<d.
$$

This proposed amendment allows the generic base size to exceed the minimal base size, as happens in many algebraic examples, while conjecturing that the gap is uniformly bounded. The source gives no resolution of this formulation.
record.source_name: James Freitag, Léo Jimenez and Rahim Moosa, “Finite-dimensional differential-algebraic permutation groups”, arXiv:2307.11220 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.11220

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2023). “In $\acf_0$ this was verified by the first and third authors in , following a strategy suggested in .”

record.title: Matrix form of Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M=(m_{ij})$ be a non-zero binary matrix of size $n\times m$ with distinct rows. For binary rows, write $M_{i-}\lor M_{j-}$ for their coordinatewise logical disjunction, and denote the columns of $M$ by $M_{-k}$. **Matrix form of Frankl's conjecture.** If for every pair of rows $M_{i-}$ and $M_{j-}$ the row $M_{i-}\lor M_{j-}$ also occurs in $M$, then there exists a column $M_{-k}$ containing at least $n/2$ ones.

This is a binary-matrix reformulation of the union-closed sets conjecture, expressing union closure as closure of the rows under coordinatewise disjunction. Its general status is open, alongside the original set-system formulation.
record.source_name: Mohammad Javad Moghaddas Mehr, “A Note on the Union-closed Sets Conjecture”, arXiv:2309.01704 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01704

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Unbounded open embedding dimension for Steiner triple codes
record.statement:
A **Steiner triple system** on $n$ is a set of triples in $[n]$ in which every pair appears in a unique triple; adjoining the singletons and the empty codeword gives an associated **Steiner triple code**. For a code $\mathcal{C}$, write $\operatorname{odim}(\mathcal{C})$ for its open embedding dimension.

**Steiner triple code embedding-dimension conjecture.** For every $d\ge 1$ there exists a Steiner triple code $\mathcal{C}$ with

$$
\operatorname{odim}(\mathcal{C})\ge d.
$$

Steiner triple codes are 3-sparse and have closed embedding dimension at most five, while the Fano-plane example shows that their open embedding dimension can exceed their closed embedding dimension. The conjecture predicts that this open embedding dimension is unbounded across Steiner triple codes.
record.source_name: R. Amzi Jeffs, Henry Siegel, David Staudinger and Yiqing Wang, “Embedding dimension gaps in sparse codes”, arXiv:2309.14862 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.14862

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “We pose several open questions regarding sparse and low-degree codes. In particular, we conjecture that the open embedding dimension of certain 3-sparse codes derived from Steiner triple systems grows to infinity.”

record.title: Bounded average line-length from bounded average plane-size for matroids
record.statement: Let $M$ be a simple matroid of rank at least $6$. The average line-length is the average size of the rank-$2$ flats of $M$, and the average plane-size is the average size of its rank-$3$ flats. **Matroid line-to-plane boundedness conjecture.** For every real number $\alpha_2$, there is a real number $\alpha_3$ such that, if the average line-length of $M$ is at most $\alpha_2$, then the average plane-size is at most $\alpha_3$. The conjecture extends the discussion from complex-representable matroids to arbitrary matroids; the source notes that a bound of $6$ is best possible in the relevant context.
record.source_name: Rutger Campbell, Jim Geelen and Matthew E. Kroeker, “Average plane-size in complex-representable matroids”, arXiv:2310.02826 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: The BIG implies BIG conjecture for tournaments
record.statement: A class of tournaments $\mathcal T$ has the **$BIG\Rightarrow BIG$ property** if there exists a function $f$ such that, for every $T\in\mathcal T$, if $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\chi}}(T)\geq f(t)$, then $T$ contains disjoint subtournaments $A$ and $B$ with $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\chi}}(A),\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\chi}}(B)\geq t$ and $A\Rightarrow B$. **The BIG implies BIG conjecture.** The class of all tournaments has the $BIG\Rightarrow BIG$ property. This conjecture is attributed to Nguyen, Scott and Seymour and is presented as implying the Erdős–El-Zahar conjecture.
record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian, Pierre Charbit and Raul Lopes, “Clique number of tournaments”, arXiv:2310.04265 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Ruckle's conjecture on optimal hiding in the accumulation game
record.statement:
In the accumulation game, the hider has $d$ positive weight units of gold to distribute among $n$ boxes, and the searcher queries $k$ boxes. An optimal hiding strategy minimizes the number of queried $k$-sets whose combined gold weight is at least $1$.

**Ruckle's conjecture.** For all parameters, there exists an optimal hiding strategy in which the hider chooses $r$ boxes, hides exactly $d/r$ units of gold in each chosen box, and leaves all remaining boxes empty.
The paper notes that this conjecture is equivalent to the corresponding maximization formulation in Ruckle's work and proves it in the case $k\mid n$, but gives examples showing that nontrivial optimal strategies may occur for other parameters. The general conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Áron Jánosik, Csenge Miklós, Dániel G. Simon and Kristóf Zólomy, “Discrete and Continuous Caching Games”, arXiv:2310.13777 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13777

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Quadratic weakening of the chromatic-intersection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of labelled graphs on the vertex-set $[n]$, and let $\chi(G)$ denote chromatic number. **Quadratic chromatic-intersection conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for every $t\geq3$, if $\chi(G\cap H)\geq t$ for all $G,H\in\mathcal{F}$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq2^{\binom n2-ct^2}.
$$

This is explicitly presented as a weaker conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Rahil Baber, Natalie Behague, Asier Calbet, David Ellis, Joshua Erde, Ron Gray, Maria-Romina Ivan, Barnabás Janzer, Robert Johnson, Luka Milićević, John Talbot, Ta Sheng Tan and Belinda Wickes, “A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader's 60th birthday”, arXiv:2310.18163 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Conjecture on forbidden intervals of irredundant-base cardinalities for primitive groups
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{I}(G,\Omega)$ denote the set of cardinalities of irredundant bases of a permutation group $G$ on $\Omega$. **Forbidden-interval conjecture.** There exists an interval $X$ of positive integers, with $1\notin X$, such that no primitive permutation group $G$ on $\Omega$ satisfies

$$
X=\mathcal{I}(G,\Omega).
$$

This conjecture asserts that at least one interval excluding $1$ cannot arise as the set of irredundant-base cardinalities of a primitive permutation group. The source presents it as an open question motivated by the lack of a stronger realization conjecture for all such intervals.
record.source_name: Francesca Dalla Volta, Fabio Mastrogiacomo and Pablo Spiga, “On the cardinality of irredundant and minimal bases of finite permutation groups”, arXiv:2311.04489 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.04489

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Existence of infinite cubulable groups with fixed-point property $(\mathrm{FW}_n)$
record.statement: A group is **cubulable** if it acts properly and cocompactly on a median graph. For $n\geq 1$, $(\mathrm{FW}_n)$ denotes the fixed-point property for actions on median graphs of cubical dimension at most $n$. **Existence conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, there exists an infinite cubulable group satisfying $(\mathrm{FW}_n)$ with no proper finite-index subgroup. The surrounding discussion gives constructions of cubulable groups with fixed-point properties and explains why controlling finite-index subgroups is difficult; the existence assertion is left as an open problem.
record.source_name: Anthony Genevois, “Examples of cubulable groups with fixed-point properties”, arXiv:2311.12402 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12402

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Kostochka et al.'s super-neighborhood cycle conjecture for bigraphs
record.statement:
A **bigraph** is a bipartite graph $G=(X,Y)$ with an ordered vertex partition. For a set $S\subseteq X$, let $\mathsf{\Lambda}^2(S)$ be the vertices adjacent to at least two vertices of $S$. The graph is **snp** if, for every $S\subseteq X$ with $|S|\geq 3$, $|\mathsf{\Lambda}^2(S)|\geq |S|$ and $G[S\cup\mathsf{\Lambda}^2(S)]$ is $2$-connected.

**Kostochka et al.'s conjecture.** If a bigraph $G=(X,Y)$ is snp, then there is a cycle containing all vertices of $X$.

This is the graph-theoretic form of the conjectured equivalence between the super-neighborhood property and super-pancyclicity of hypergraphs. The conjecture is known for $|X|\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Guantao Chen, Mikhail Lavrov, Yuying Ma, Yimo Su and Jennifer Vandenbussche, “Bipartite graphs with the double Hall property”, arXiv:2502.10903 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2310.05248](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05248).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10903

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
